messages:
maria (product): Quick sync — we need a firm decision on our long-term routing + multi-tenant isolation model so sales + infra can commit to Dedicated/Private SLAs. high-level ask: phased approach, clear launch criteria, and a migration path for 3 large tenants (acme, flux, beacon).

devon (eng-arch): Proposal sketch: define isolation "levels":
- L0: fully shared runtime, tenant-level soft quotas + pref routing
- L1: logical isolation (dedicated queues, soft resource reservations, prefix KV caching isolated)
- L2: hard isolation (dedicated pods/nodes per tenant, strict network/data plane separation)

devon (eng-arch): DSL for routing policy (very rough):
```
route {
  match tenant in [acme,beacon] -> prefer region(us-east-1), isolation L1
  match workload.type == "sensitive" -> isolation L2, require KMS
  fallback -> shared_pool
}
```

kevin (sre): Good. Need to attach measurable launch criteria for each level otherwise ops will be stuck forever. Suggest:
- L1 launch: p95 latency delta vs baseline < +12ms, error rate change < 0.05%, cost delta <= 15% for pilot tenants
- L2 launch: p95 delta < +20ms, full audit logs enabled, KMS-integrated, documented failover playbook

sara (eng-ml): For model routing, add model-variant affinity so heavy KV cache models can be colocated. For L1 we should allow "cache partitions" per tenant to keep short-term perf gains.

devon (eng-arch): Migration path idea: three phases per-tenant:
1) Pilot (L1 soft): migrate traffic 5-10% with canary, monitor p95, tail tokens, regen rates
2) Ramp: 50% traffic after 48h stable signals
3) Cutover to L1/L2 depending on contract

kevin (sre): Observability signals to gate ramps:
- token-level cost spike > X%
- p99 increase sustained > 30s
- queue depth > threshold for > 10m
- KV cache hit rate drop > 10%
If any trigger trips, auto-roll back 10% and pager oncall.

maria (product): Launch criteria we need for sales: SLA doc + cost delta envelope + migration timeline commitment. Proposed minimums for GA:
- Offer L1 as GA for Dedicated with SLA 99.9% region availability
- L2 GA only as enterprise private option (onboarding + runbook)
- Migration: typical customer onboarding 2-6 weeks (pilot->ramp->cutover)

devon (eng-arch): One open question: routing policy language — keep it simple key/value match vs full policy engine (Rego). My vote: start with declarative small DSL (like snippet above) and compile to policy checks; if complexity grows we can slot in a full PDP later.

kevin (sre): Cost modelling: estimate worst-case infra delta per tenant for L1 vs L0 and L2 vs L1. If L1 increases cost > 18% for a tenant we should require a signed shared-cost uplift. Need finance to probe.

sara (eng-ml): Also flag model licensing and quantization differences per tenant. Some tenants will require FP16 GPUs -> drives node class selection. Add that to the templated migration checklist.

infra-bot: [deploy-check] infra config validated for branch "isolation-phases-v1" — 4 checks passed, 1 flaky (policy-compiler tests).

maria (product): Next actions:
- devon: draft RFC with the L0/L1/L2 semantics, DSL primer, and migration playbook (due EOD Fri)
- kevin: cost delta spreadsheet + gating signals (end of week)
- sara: list of model-specific constraints we must support for L1 (GPU class, KV cache sizes)

devon (eng-arch): acked. I'll include a short appendix: customer migration case study (acme) simulating traffic shift and cost.

kevin (sre): +1. Please include rollback steps and runbook snippets.

maria (product): Great — if no objections we'll slot this for product review next Tues. :thumbsup:

sara (eng-ml): :thumbsup:

devon (eng-arch): one more note — we should include a "soft quota" enforcement mode that acts as advisory for the first 2 weeks of a migration to avoid false positives.

maria (product): Good call. ok wrapping up — thanks everyone.
